newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Finland want EU talks to end on time.
newsitem.headline: France, Finland want EU talks to end on time.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and Finland's Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen urged their European Union partners on Thursday to complete the 15-member bloc's review of its institutions as scheduled by mid-1997.
"We should make an effort to stick to the timetable so that we could then proceed to the enlargement of the European Union," Lipponen told reporters after meeting Chirac.

A spokesman for Chirac quoted the president as saying he hoped the work of a special summit this weekend in Dublin would allow the timetable to be respected and that a list of issues and solutions would be drawn up "to give foreign ministers a mission".

The summit is being held to meet the concerns of some in the EU -- notably Chirac -- that the so-called intergovernmental conference (IGC), a treaty review preparing the bloc for enlargement, has become bogged down.
"The president also expressed his willingness to increase bilateral contacts with Finland and I expressed our wish that France could engage more in cooperation around the Baltic sea," Lipponen added.
